name: v2-smoke
note: Smoke batch for the v2 engine: every non-ad shell (legacy + v2) at 1080x1350 (instagram), 1000x1500 (pinterest) and 1080x1920 (story), plus a carousel and a receipt reel entry. Sequenced as a valid plan per channel so the diversity and copy gates run on it. Never scheduled.

posts.head: One receipt. Four dinners.
posts.title: One grocery receipt, four weeknight dinners
posts.text: Scan the receipt from Sunday and iEatz maps it to the week: tacos Monday, fried rice Tuesday, a big salad Wednesday, soup from the bones on Sunday.

posts.head: Ten dinners are already on your shelves.
posts.body: Scan the receipt and iEatz reads your kitchen back to you, starting with what expires first.
posts.title: Ten dinners hiding on your pantry shelves
posts.text: The average scan finds about ten dinners in groceries people already own. The shelves were full the whole time.

posts.cap: Nothing new came home. $0.00 spent. The bowl was on the top shelf.
posts.photoClaim: open fridge full of produce above a bowl of greens with eggs and avocado
posts.title: Same fridge, two days later: a bowl of greens and eggs
posts.text: Sunday the fridge looked like nothing. Tuesday it was a bowl of greens, soft eggs and avocado, and nobody went to the store.

posts.head: Pesto pasta salad that keeps till Friday
posts.method: Cook the pasta, toss it warm with pesto, fold in tomatoes and greens once it cools.
posts.photoClaim: bowl of farfalle with pesto, cherry tomatoes and greens
posts.title: Pesto pasta salad for weekday lunches
posts.text: Farfalle, pesto, cherry tomatoes, a handful of greens. Make it Sunday and it still tastes right on Friday.

posts.head: The 5:45 text, retired.

msgs.text: what do u want for dinner
it says we have everything for fried rice. 20 min

posts.foot: iEatz reads the receipt so the 5:45 text ends in a pan.
posts.photoClaim: hands stirring fried rice in a pan by a kitchen window
posts.title: The 5:45 what-do-you-want-for-dinner text, answered
posts.text: Every household has this text thread. Ours now ends with fried rice in a pan twenty minutes later.

posts.head: Receipt in, dinners out.
posts.title: Watch a grocery receipt turn into three dinners
posts.text: Fourteen items from Thursday: baked penne, lemon ricotta pasta and tomato soup, printed in order of what goes off first.

posts.statBody: When the recipe starts from groceries you already bought, the math works.
posts.title: About $6 a serving for a healthy dinner
posts.text: Dinner from what you already bought comes out around six dollars a serving. The expensive meal is the one you order after forgetting what was in the fridge.

posts.head: Dinner is in here
posts.photoClaim: open fridge with eggs, sausages, a jar of garlic and strawberries
posts.title: Dinner is already in your fridge
posts.text: Eggs up top, sausages and a jar of garlic in the middle. That is a frittata, and it is already paid for.

posts.head: Four dinners from one rotisserie chicken
posts.title: Four dinners from one rotisserie chicken
posts.text: Tacos, fried rice, a chopped salad, then broth from the bones. One nine-dollar bird covers four weeknights.

posts.quote: Three weeks in and I haven't ordered takeout once.
posts.photoClaim: person slicing vegetables at a kitchen counter
posts.title: Three weeks without takeout
posts.text: Ashly H. on three weeks of cooking what was already in her kitchen, from the App Store reviews.

posts.head: Chop the cilantro before it wilts
posts.photoClaim: hands chopping cilantro on a wooden board
posts.title: Chop the cilantro before it wilts
posts.text: Two minutes with a knife on Sunday and the cilantro lasts into next week. Freeze the rest in olive oil.

posts.head: Soup night, minus the missing onion.
posts.cap: When a recipe needs one thing you don't have, iEatz sends it to an Instacart cart in a tap.
posts.photoClaim: real iEatz screen listing missing items next to an Instacart cart
posts.title: The missing onion goes straight to an Instacart cart
posts.text: One missing item used to stall the whole recipe. Now it goes to a cart and the soup keeps going.

posts.head: Wednesday spaghetti, twenty minutes flat
posts.photoClaim: plate of spaghetti with mushrooms and herbs
posts.title: Twenty-minute Wednesday spaghetti
posts.text: Spaghetti, mushrooms, garlic and whatever herbs are left. One skillet, twenty minutes, Wednesday handled.

posts.head: Pantry to plate in fifteen.
posts.photoClaim: pantry shelves of packaged groceries and tacos with chickpeas and lime
posts.title: Pantry to plate in fifteen minutes
posts.text: The shelf nobody looks at has tacos on it. Chickpeas, a lime and tortillas, about two dollars a plate.

posts.head: Green sauce for everything
posts.method: Blitz everything until smooth and spoon it over anything beige.
posts.title: Green herb yogurt sauce that keeps a week
posts.text: Soft herbs, yogurt, lemon and garlic in a blender. It rescues the herbs and every plain dinner after.

posts.head: The 6:30 kitchen, back on schedule
posts.sub: Evenings run smoother when nobody has to decide what dinner is.
posts.photoClaim: woman cooking at a stove in a white kitchen
posts.title: The 6:30 kitchen, back on schedule
posts.text: A school-night kitchen at 6:30 with dinner already decided. The quiet part is nobody asking what we are having.

posts.quote: I just cook what's already in my kitchen.
posts.name: Ashly H.
posts.title: Cooking what is already in the kitchen
posts.text: The second half of Ashly H.'s review, and the whole idea of the app in one line.

posts.body: Most weeknight dinners land in about fifteen minutes when they start from what you have.
posts.title: Fridge to table in about fifteen minutes
posts.text: Most iEatz weeknight dinners land in about fifteen minutes because the shopping step is gone.

posts.title: Four weeknight bowls from one grocery run
posts.text: Swipe for four bowls: grain bowl, kimchi rice, chickpea bowl and a green bean power bowl. Save it for the next grocery run.

slides.head: Four bowls from one grocery run.
slides.body: Swipe. Same bag of groceries, four weeknights, no repeats.

slides.head: Monday: chicken grain bowl
slides.method: Warm the rice, slice the chicken, pile it all in one bowl.
slides.photoClaim: wooden bowl of sliced chicken, rice and chickpeas

slides.head: Tuesday: kimchi rice bowl
slides.method: Leftover rice under a heap of kimchi. Fry an egg if you have one.
slides.photoClaim: hands holding a bowl of rice topped with kimchi

slides.head: Wednesday: chickpea bowl
slides.method: Crisp the chickpeas in a hot pan, then everything cold on top.
slides.photoClaim: bowl of chickpeas, cucumber, tomato and greens

slides.head: Thursday: green bean power bowl
slides.method: Blanch the beans, fluff the couscous, dress it all with lemon.
slides.photoClaim: plate of green beans, couscous and tomatoes

msgs.text: nope. eggs, yogurt, half a box of veg

posts.foot: The fridge had dinner in it the whole time.
posts.photoClaim: open fridge with stocked shelves, yogurt cups and a box of vegetables
posts.title: The fridge had dinner in it the whole time
posts.text: Eggs, yogurt and half a box of vegetables is shakshuka. The fridge was never empty.
